Facts:
- Fulgencio Batista was a Cuban military leader who led the military coup that removed Cuban President Carlos Prío Socarrás from office.
- Osvaldo Farrés composed the song "Quizás, Quizás, Quizás."
- Cuban President Carlos Prío Socarrás served as inspiration for Osvaldo Farrés when he composed "Quizás, Quizás, Quizás."

This chunk is about:
- People: Mary Tarrero-Serrano, Carlos Prío Socarrás, Fulgencio Batista, Osvaldo Farrés
- Roles: Cuban First Lady, President of Cuba, dictator
- Events: 1952 Cuban military coup, Cuban Revolution
- Works: “Quizás, Quizás, Quizás”

Facts:
- Fulgencio Batista was born on January 16, 1901, and was originally named Rubén Zaldívar.
- Carlos Prío Socarrás was born on July 14, 1903.
- Fulgencio Batista was the elected President of Cuba from 1940 to 1944.
- Carlos Prío Socarrás was the President of Cuba from 1948 until March 10, 1952.
- Mary Tarrero-Serrano was the second wife of Cuban President Carlos Prío Socarrás.
- Mary Tarrero-Serrano served as Cuban First Lady during Carlos Prío Socarrás’s presidency.
- On March 10, 1952, Fulgencio Batista led the military coup that deposed Carlos Prío Socarrás three months before new elections were to be held.
- Fulgencio Batista ruled Cuba as a U.S.-backed dictator from 1952 to 1959.
- Fulgencio Batista was overthrown during the Cuban Revolution.
- Osvaldo Farrés received help and inspiration for the lyrics of “Quizás, Quizás, Quizás” from Cuban First Lady Mary Tarrero-Serrano.
- Fulgencio Batista died on August 6, 1973.
- Carlos Prío Socarrás died on April 5, 1977.
